## The status badge {#status-legend}

Each conjecture carries one badge summarizing where it stands. It's a deterministic function of six fields tracked in the page's `status:` frontmatter — never hand-picked. A machine-checked proof of an unmatched formalization certifies nothing about the conjecture itself, so the badge treats *whether the formal statement actually matches the informal one* as a first-class signal, not an afterthought. Click any badge, anywhere on the site, to come back to this legend.

### Symbol key

```{=html}
<table class="cj-badge-legend">
<tbody>
<tr><th colspan="2">Outer ring — statement grade σ (0–5)</th></tr>
<tr><td><svg viewBox='0 0 32 32' width='24' height='24' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><circle cx='16' cy='16' r='13' fill='none' stroke-width='4' class='cj-ring-0'/></svg></td><td>Pale → saturated green, lightest (0) to darkest (5): 0–1 = only an informal statement exists; 2–3 = formalized in Lean but not yet matched against the informal statement; 4–5 = formalized <em>and</em> matched</td></tr>
<tr><td><svg viewBox='0 0 32 32' width='24' height='24' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><circle cx='16' cy='16' r='13' fill='none' stroke-width='4' class='cj-ring-3' stroke-dasharray='1,3'/></svg></td><td>Dotted ring — formalized, but <strong>not yet matched</strong> against the informal statement (the dangerous cell: a proof about this statement proves nothing about the conjecture until it's matched)</td></tr>
<tr><td><svg viewBox='0 0 32 32' width='24' height='24' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><circle cx='16' cy='16' r='13' fill='none' stroke-width='4' class='cj-ring-3' stroke-dasharray='5,3'/></svg></td><td>Dashed ring — an AI checked the formalization matches the informal statement</td></tr>
<tr><td><svg viewBox='0 0 32 32' width='24' height='24' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><circle cx='16' cy='16' r='13' fill='none' stroke-width='4' class='cj-ring-5'/></svg></td><td>Solid ring — a human checked the formalization matches the informal statement</td></tr>
<tr><th colspan="2">Inner disc — proof grade π (0–4)</th></tr>
<tr><td><svg viewBox='0 0 32 32' width='24' height='24' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><circle cx='16' cy='16' r='13' class='cj-disc-0'/></svg></td><td>White (0, nothing attempted) → saturated green (4, machine-checked): a blank disc means no proof attempt at all, distinct from even the palest green. Levels 1–4 use the same green as the ring — the whole badge reads "more green" as a conjecture progresses, regardless of which side is moving</td></tr>
<tr><th colspan="2">Centre glyph — restates the proof grade π as text, independent of colour</th></tr>
<tr><td><svg viewBox='0 0 32 32' width='24' height='24' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><text x='16' y='17' text-anchor='middle' dominant-baseline='central' class='cj-glyph' font-size='14'>–</text></svg></td><td>π = 0 — no proof attempt yet</td></tr>
<tr><td><svg viewBox='0 0 32 32' width='24' height='24' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><text x='16' y='17' text-anchor='middle' dominant-baseline='central' class='cj-glyph' font-size='14'>·</text></svg></td><td>π = 1 — AI draft, not yet independently reviewed</td></tr>
<tr><td><svg viewBox='0 0 32 32' width='24' height='24' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><text x='16' y='17' text-anchor='middle' dominant-baseline='central' class='cj-glyph' font-size='14'>•</text></svg></td><td>π = 2 — one of {draft author, reviewer} is human</td></tr>
<tr><td><svg viewBox='0 0 32 32' width='24' height='24' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><text x='16' y='17' text-anchor='middle' dominant-baseline='central' class='cj-glyph' font-size='14'>●</text></svg></td><td>π = 3 — human draft, human-reviewed, still not formalized</td></tr>
<tr><td><svg viewBox='0 0 32 32' width='24' height='24' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><text x='16' y='17' text-anchor='middle' dominant-baseline='central' class='cj-glyph' font-size='14'>✓</text></svg></td><td>π = 4 — machine-checked (a completed Lean proof, not just a <code>sorry</code>); who wrote it no longer matters, the kernel is the arbiter</td></tr>
<tr><th colspan="2">Seal</th></tr>
<tr><td><svg viewBox='0 0 32 32' width='24' height='24' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><circle cx='16' cy='16' r='15' fill='none' stroke-width='1.5' class='cj-seal'/><circle cx='16' cy='16' r='13' fill='none' stroke-width='4' class='cj-ring-5'/></svg></td><td>Thin gold outer halo — appears only when σ ≥ 4 (human-matched) <em>and</em> π = 4 (machine-checked): the fully de&#8209;Bruijn&#8209;verified state</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
```

**Statement side** (outer ring): `statement_informal` (ai/human — who wrote the informal write-up), `statement_formal` (open/ai/human — has it been formalized in Lean, and by whom), `statement_match` (open/ai/human — has that formalization been checked against the informal statement, and by whom). These combine into a statement grade σ from 0 (AI-written, unformalized) to 5 (human-written, human-formalized, human-matched).

**Proof side** (inner disc): `proof_informal` (open/ai/human), `proof_review` (ai/human — vacuous once a formal proof exists), `proof_formal` (open/ai/human — a completed Lean proof, not just a `sorry`). These combine into a proof grade π from 0 (no attempt) to 4 (machine-checked — once a proof is formally verified, the Lean kernel is the arbiter, so *who* wrote it no longer affects the grade, only a caption detail).

**Reading the badge:** the outer ring's colour is the statement grade; its line style is the match status redundantly (dotted = unmatched, dashed = AI-matched, solid = human-matched) so it survives greyscale. The inner disc's colour is the proof grade, with a centre glyph (`– · • ● ✓`) as a second redundant channel. A thin gold outer halo (a seal) appears only when the statement is human-matched *and* the proof is machine-checked — the fully de-Bruijn-verified state. Hovering any badge shows the full plain-English status as a tooltip.


To update a statement's status: edit the six `status.*` fields in its `c/<id>/index.qmd` frontmatter, then run `python3 scripts/status_badge.py` from the repo root to regenerate the badge (`status_badge:` in the frontmatter, and the inline copy between the `<!-- status:start -->` / `<!-- status:end -->` markers in the body); never hand-edit `status_badge:` itself.

## Beyond the badge

The badge is deliberately narrow: it's a pure function of the six fields above, and always will be. It can't say a result is actually settled before it's machine-checked, and it can't say what's actually been tried. Three things next to it cover that:

**`status_summary`**, one required sentence, shown next to the badge in every listing table, so a facet page is scannable without opening every statement.

**The `## Status` section**, on every statement page: free prose covering what a badge can't, including what's been tried, what's known for special cases, where the argument is stuck, which lemma is load-bearing, and what a resolution would imply. No length cap.

**`### Open obligations`**, inside `## Status`: a markdown task list of the concrete outstanding items (unverified steps, unaudited files, unmatched formalizations, missing sanity lemmas). The open count is its own column in listing tables.

**`category`** also matters here: `research-solved` and `test` statements exist on the site precisely because the badge alone would make a proven-but-unformalized result look identical to an untouched one. [c/0004](/c/0004/) is a real example: proven informally, badge still low, with `category: research-solved` and its `## Status` section being what actually says so.

In short: **the badge summarizes, the prose explains.** Neither substitutes for the other.
